answer: Topological Cutoff Quorum. An agent's reach is capped by the number of distinct routing neighborhoods it touches: each new identity must anchor to a sparse reef of relay nodes, and cluster density is measured against a reference tundra where honest agents stay scattered. Sybil clusters collapse into one dense garden, so their quorum weight is divided by internal edge overlap. Cost: each fake identity needs fresh relay links across separated neighborhoods, forcing real bandwidth and latency per node.
